questions.q: In the Castlebridge invoice-processing flow, what does Stage 3's Condition check?
options: Whether the email has an attachment at all
The confidence score of an extracted field, routing low-confidence extractions to manual entry instead of continuing
Whether the invoice total is exactly zero
The sender's email domain
questions.explain: Stage 3 checks the ShipmentID confidence score from the document processing model. Below the threshold, the flow routes to manual entry rather than trusting an uncertain extraction.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the JSON-output prompt in Stage 4 of the flow?
options: To re-extract the same fields a second time for no reason
To reason about whether the extracted data is internally consistent, such as checking line items against the stated invoice total
To translate the invoice into another language
To replace the document processing model entirely
questions.explain: The JSON-output prompt cross-checks the extracted total against the line-item table, catching inconsistencies a confident-but-wrong extraction might miss.

questions.q: Why does the flow have two separate branching points (a confidence check and a totals-match check) instead of just one?
options: Redundancy with no real purpose
They catch two different failure modes: the model being unsure of its extraction, versus the model being confident but factually inconsistent
Power Automate requires at least two Conditions in every flow
One branch is for text and the other is only for images
questions.explain: A low confidence score and a totals mismatch are different problems — one is the model's own uncertainty, the other is a confident extraction that doesn't add up. Each needs its own check.

questions.q: What should Castlebridge test this flow against, beyond a single clean sample invoice?
options: Nothing else — one clean test is sufficient
A deliberately messy batch: a blurry scan, a new carrier's template, an invoice with a line-item total that's slightly off
Only invoices with zero dollar totals
Only invoices in a language other than English
questions.explain: Testing only against one clean sample won't reveal either failure mode (low confidence or inconsistent totals) that the flow's branches exist to catch.

questions.q: What is the broader lesson this capstone flow demonstrates, beyond the specific Castlebridge scenario?
options: AI Builder actions must always be used completely on their own, never combined with Conditions or Approvals
AI Builder actions compose with ordinary flow logic like any other action, and reliable AI flows plan for the AI step being wrong
Document processing models never need human review under any circumstance
JSON output prompts can replace triggers entirely
questions.explain: The capstone's real point is that AI Builder steps are just actions that combine with triggers, conditions, and approvals — and that the most reliable flows assume an AI step might be wrong and branch for it.
